name: Refugee Status / Political Asylum

requirements.blocker_text: Ley de Migracion y Extranjeria (Decreto 208-2003), Article 42: refugee criteria cover both classic 1951-Convention grounds (persecution based on race, religion, nationality, social group, or political opinion) and a broader Cartagena-style ground of threats from 'generalized, grave and continuous violence.' Article 8(20) assigns recognition authority to the migration authority (INM). Practical process (per UNHCR's Honduras guidance): file at any INM delegation or Migrant Care Center (CAMI); confidential interview with an INM human-rights officer; biometric registration; a free, renewable 90-day 'Autorizacion de Permanencia Temporal' while the case is pending; INM's human-rights unit analyzes the case and presents it to the Refugee Commission; decision notified by phone/email with a 10-day appeal window on denial; approved applicants register in the National Registry of Foreigners for refugee identification. Article 46 bars deportation of asylum seekers or recognized refugees except for security/public-order reasons.
requirements.fix_path: File a refugee claim at an INM delegation or CAMI and complete the interview/biometric/Refugee Commission review process.

requirements.blocker_text: Article 52 provides a separate territorial-asylum track for political persecution, human rights violations, or politically-natured crimes, decided by the Secretary of State for Governance and Justice rather than INM's refugee process.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for territorial asylum through the Secretariat of Governance and Justice.

outcome.duration_length: indefinite, temporary permit renewable 90 days at a time pending resolution

sources.title: Instituto Nacional de Migracion de Honduras -- hosted primary legal text of Decreto 208-2003, Articles 8(20), 42, 46, 47 and 52 (refugee criteria, recognition authority, non-refoulement, family reunification, and separate territorial-asylum track)
UNHCR Help Honduras -- practical 7-step asylum procedure, 90-day renewable temporary permit, 10-day appeal window, free of charge

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Honduras). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- the hard requirements (both refugee-status criteria and the separate territorial-asylum track) are sourced directly to the government-hosted primary statutory text, tier 1, corroborated by UNHCR's own country guidance (tier 2) for the practical process and timelines. GENUINE, DISTINCTIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING: Honduras runs TWO parallel protection tracks under one law -- ordinary refugee status (broader Cartagena-style 'generalized violence' ground included, decided by INM with Refugee Commission input) and a separate territorial political-asylum track decided directly by the Secretariat of Governance and Justice (Article 52) -- a bifurcation not seen in this exact form in this dataset's other asylum files. work_rights set 'restricted': the sources describe the temporary permanence authorization and identity/travel documentation but did not confirm automatic open work rights for either track. leads_to_pr and leads_to_citizenship set false: no source reviewed described a defined conversion path from refugee/asylum status to permanent residence or citizenship -- disclosed as an open gap rather than assumed to follow the standard 3-year 'other foreigners' naturalization track. family_can_work left null since Article 47's family-reunification right was confirmed but independent work authorization for joining relatives was not addressed.
